newsitem.title: USA: Bush praises Deng for opening up China economy.
newsitem.headline: Bush praises Deng for opening up China economy.

text.p: Former U.S. President George Bush on Wednesday praised the late Deng Xiaoping as a "remarkable leader" who brought benefits to millions of his countrymen by opening up China's economic system.

Bush, who was U.S. ambassador to China from 1974 to 1976 and met with Deng in China shortly after becoming U.S. president in 1989, said Deng "played a critical role in establishing strong ties between our two countries."
Deng, who had been in failing health, died on Wednesday at the age of 93 from complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection.
"While we were not always in accord, Deng without a doubt made a powerful contribution to a foundation for enduring peace and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region," Bush said in a statement.
"His foresight and vision has also brought dramatic change to China, enabling millions to begin to enjoy the benefits of a more open, market-oriented system," Bush said.
He said he hoped that Deng's "many accomplishments will flourish in China for decades to come and that we all continue to build on his legacy of mutual understanding and respect."
